cl_opi_tramadol_overdose.q: Can tramadol cause seizures, and what happens in an overdose?
cl_opi_tramadol_overdose.short: In overdoses, seizures are common. 11 in 100 people treated at one Australian unit had them, and about 35 in 100 in Iran. Some had trouble breathing too.
cl_opi_tramadol_overdose.but: These were overdoses, often with other pills too. No one checked the risk at normal doses.
how: At one Australian hospital unit, 8 of 71 people treated for a tramadol overdose had seizures. That was 2 of the 20 who took only tramadol, and 6 of the 51 who took other pills too. Some came almost a day later.

18 in 100 had breathing trouble with low oxygen, and 5 went into a coma (3 of them had also taken an older type of antidepressant). Those who said they took more had more seizures and breathing trouble. Nobody died.
No one met the criteria for serotonin syndrome. With 71 people, that only rules out rates above about 5 in 100. Earlier reported cases mostly involved tramadol taken with antidepressants.
In 23 Iranian hospital studies, about 35 in 100 had seizures, but single studies ranged from 12 to 69 in 100. About 7 in 1,000 died in hospital; one study had 100 in 1,000.
cl_opi_tramadol_overdose.rate: Hospital records only: one Australian unit and many Iranian hospitals. Amounts weren't checked by lab tests, many people took other medicines too, and the figures differ a lot between countries.

cl_opi_tramadol_withdrawal.q: Is tramadol withdrawal different from other opioids?
cl_opi_tramadol_withdrawal.short: Sometimes, going by reports. In US reports from 1995 to 2000, most looked like usual opioid withdrawal. But about 1 in 8 also had panic, confusion, numbness or hallucinations.
cl_opi_tramadol_withdrawal.but: It's only cases people chose to report. And no one compared it with stopping other opioids.
how: Of 1,248 side-effect reports in tramadol's first five years in the US, 422 were withdrawal after stopping. Most were the usual kind: cramps, diarrhoea, goose bumps, a runny nose, sweating, poor sleep.

55 (about 1 in 8) had more: bad anxiety or panic (1 in 3 of them), confusion or feeling unreal (1 in 4), numbness or tingling (1 in 4), or hallucinations (1 in 5). The researchers say this could be mistaken for psychosis.
Most people whose dose was known had taken no more than the recommended daily maximum, and many had used tramadol only a few days. Doctors called most cases mild, usually over in 2 or 3 days.

How often withdrawal happens is unknown: the researchers cite an estimate that only about 1 in 10 side effects get reported. The drug's maker paid for the study. A review of Iranian studies found just two case reports of it.
cl_opi_tramadol_withdrawal.rate: One set of US side-effect reports, which catch only some cases, sorted by a committee the drug's maker paid for. Nobody compared people stopping tramadol with people stopping other opioids.

prescription-opioids.statement: With too much tramadol, seizures only happen if other drugs were taken too.
prescription-opioids.why: In one Australian study, 2 of 20 people who took only tramadol had seizures, against 6 of 51 who took other pills too. These were overdoses, not normal doses.

prescription-opioids.statement: Too much tramadol won't affect your breathing.
prescription-opioids.why: In one Australian study of 71 overdoses, 18 in 100 people had breathing trouble with low oxygen. Many had taken other pills too.

prescription-opioids.statement: When people stop tramadol, it always feels like the usual opioid withdrawal.
prescription-opioids.why: In US reports from 1995 to 2000, about 1 in 8 cases also had panic, confusion, numbness or hallucinations. These were reported cases only, so how often it happens is unknown.
